input.ground_truth: Another interesting thing about most sirens is that they all use the tritone (_URL_0_) in some way. This note is perticularly useful for sirens because it is so ugly that you can't not notice it. Most trains use this note exclusively because it creates so much dissonance that you will notice it over even your car stereo.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How do sirens on police cars/fire trucks/ambulances/tornado siren/etc work?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a toy that makes a loud "WHEEEEEEEELLL!" sound when you press a button. Sirens on police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, and tornado alarms are like that toy, but much, much louder and bigger!

When someone needs to tell everyone "Hey, pay attention! Something important is happening!" they turn on the siren. The siren has a special part inside that spins really fast and makes a loud noise. This noise is loud and scary on purpose, so people know to look and listen right away.

For example:
- Police cars use sirens to let everyone know they are coming to help or catch a bad guy.
- Fire trucks use sirens to tell people there is a fire and they are coming to help.
- Ambulances use sirens to get to sick or hurt people as fast as they can.
- Tornado sirens make a super loud noise to tell everyone to go inside and be safe because a big storm is coming.

So, sirens are like a giant alarm clock or a big "LOOK AT ME!" sign that uses sound to get your attention!
